title: The cat who opens doors
setting: Saturday evening. Mai is away for the weekend, and Sora, Kenta's flatmate, is staying at her flat to look after her cat, Mochi. Mai phones to see how it's going.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: もしもし、ソラくん？モチ、大丈夫？
lines.kana: もしもし、そらくん？もち、だいじょうぶ？

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, daijoubu da yo. demo ne, heya no doa, shimete mo shimete mo aku n da yo.
lines.ja: うん、大丈夫だよ。でもね、部屋のドア、閉めても閉めても開くんだよ。
lines.kana: うん、だいじょうぶだよ。でもね、へやのどあ、しめてもしめてもあくんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, she's fine. But listen, the door to the room keeps opening, however many times I shut it.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.english: Huh? Mochi? What do you mean?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mochi ne, jibun de doa akeru no. kekkou atama ii n da yo.
lines.ja: モチね、自分でドア開けるの。けっこう頭いいんだよ。
lines.kana: もちね、じぶんでどああけるの。けっこうあたまいいんだよ。
lines.english: Mochi opens doors by herself. She's pretty clever, you know.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, neko ga doa akeru no? uso!
lines.ja: え、猫がドア開けるの？うそ！
lines.kana: え、ねこがどああけるの？うそ！
lines.english: What, a cat that opens doors? No way!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto da yo. dakara, genkan no doa wa kagi kakete ne. soto ni dechau kara.
lines.ja: ほんとだよ。だから、玄関のドアは鍵かけてね。外に出ちゃうから。
lines.kana: ほんとだよ。だから、げんかんのどあはかぎかけてね。そとにでちゃうから。
lines.english: It's true. So lock the front door, okay? Otherwise she'll get out.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, yabai. doa wa shimeta kedo, kagi kaketa kke?
lines.ja: あ、やばい。ドアは閉めたけど、鍵かけたっけ？
lines.kana: あ、やばい。どあはしめたけど、かぎかけたっけ？
lines.english: Uh-oh. I shut the door, but did I lock it?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, chotto mite kite! doa, honto ni shimatteru?
lines.ja: え、ちょっと見てきて！ドア、ほんとに閉まってる？
lines.kana: え、ちょっとみてきて！どあ、ほんとにしまってる？
lines.english: What? Go and check! Is the door really shut?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, daijoubu. doa shimatteru. kagi mo kakatteru yo.
lines.ja: あ、大丈夫。ドア閉まってる。鍵もかかってるよ。
lines.kana: あ、だいじょうぶ。どあしまってる。かぎもかかってるよ。
lines.english: Oh, it's fine. The door's shut. And it's locked, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mou, bikkuri shita. de, mochi wa ima doko?
lines.ja: もう、びっくりした。で、モチは今どこ？
lines.kana: もう、びっくりした。で、もちはいまどこ？
lines.english: Geez, you scared me. So where's Mochi now?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: doko kana. a! ima, heya no doa ga aita!
lines.ja: どこかな。あ！今、部屋のドアが開いた！
lines.kana: どこかな。あ！いま、へやのどあがあいた！
lines.english: Where is she, I wonder. Oh! The door to the room just opened!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: doa aita? sore, mochi da yo.
lines.ja: ドア開いた？それ、モチだよ。
lines.kana: どああいた？それ、もちだよ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto da! mochi ga doa aketa! sugoi!
lines.ja: ほんとだ！モチがドア開けた！すごい！
lines.kana: ほんとだ！もちがどああけた！すごい！
lines.english: You're right! Mochi opened the door! That's amazing!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ne? dakara, heya no doa wa mou shimenakute ii yo. demo, genkan wa kagi kakete ne!
lines.ja: ね？だから、部屋のドアはもう閉めなくていいよ。でも、玄関は鍵かけてね！
lines.kana: ね？だから、へやのどあはもうしめなくていいよ。でも、げんかんはかぎかけてね！
lines.english: See? So you don't need to shut the room door anymore. But lock the front door!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: だから、鍵かかってるって！
lines.kana: だから、かぎかかってるって！

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai hai. ashita uchi ni kaeru kara, mochi o yoroshiku ne.
lines.ja: はいはい。明日うちに帰るから、モチをよろしくね。
lines.kana: はいはい。あしたうちにかえるから、もちをよろしくね。
lines.english: Okay, okay. I'll be home tomorrow, so look after Mochi for me till then.

questions.english: What happens in this phone call?

choices.english: Sora forgot to lock Mai's front door, and Mochi got out of the flat.
Sora keeps opening the room door to find Mochi, so Mai tells him to stop.
Mochi has been opening the room door herself, and the front door turns out to be safely locked.

questions.explanation: Line 2: the room door keeps opening however often Sora shuts it. Line 5: Mai explains that Mochi opens doors by herself (jibun de doa akeru), and in line 7 tells him to lock the front door so she can't get out. Lines 8-10: Sora isn't sure he locked it, checks, and finds the door shut and locked (doa shimatteru, kagi mo kakatteru). Lines 12-14: the room door opens again, and Sora sees Mochi do it (mochi ga doa aketa). A is wrong: the front door was shut and locked (line 10), and Mochi was in the flat (line 14). B is wrong: Sora is the one shutting the room door (line 2), Mochi is the one opening it, and Mai tells him he doesn't need to shut it anymore (line 15).

questions.english: You're carrying a big box into Kenta's flat with both hands. Kenta sees you and asks, "daijoubu? tetsudau?" (You okay? Want a hand?) Ask him to open the door for you.
questions.kana: だいじょうぶ？てつだう？
questions.answer: Ask him to open the door with akeru plus kureru or moraeru: un, gomen, doa akete kureru?

modelAnswers.ja: うん、ごめん、ドア開けてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, sorry, could you open the door for me?

modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。じゃあ、ドア開けてもらえる？
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. Could you get the door, then?

questions.explanation: Someone opening a door is doa (o) akeru, so a request is doa akete, made softer with kureru or moraeru. Mochi is the one doing it in lines 5 and 14 (jibun de doa akeru, mochi ga doa aketa). Not doa aite: aku is what the door does with nobody doing it (line 12: heya no doa ga aita), so you can't ask a person to do it.

questions.english: Mai asks how Mochi is. What does Sora say about the door to the room?
questions.ja: ソラくんは部屋のドアについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんはへやのどあについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa heya no doa ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: However many times I close the room door (tojiru, as with eyes or a book), it opens.
choices.romaji: heya no doa, tojite mo tojite mo aku n da yo.

choices.english: However many times I shut the room door, it opens.
choices.romaji: heya no doa, shimete mo shimete mo aku n da yo.

choices.english: However many times the room door shuts, it opens.
choices.romaji: heya no doa, shimatte mo shimatte mo aku n da yo.

questions.explanation: Line 2: shimete mo shimete mo, 'however many times I shut it'. Sora is the one shutting it, so the verb is shimeru, as again in line 8 (doa wa shimeta kedo). A, tojiru, is the dictionary's 'close', but it's for eyes, books and apps; doors are shimeru. C, shimatte mo, is shimaru, what the door does by itself or how it is (line 10: doa shimatteru). Sora is talking about what he keeps doing, so it's shimeru.

questions.english: While Sora is looking for Mochi, he suddenly says "a! ima, heya no doa ga aita!" What happened?
questions.ja: 部屋のドアは、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: へやのどあは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: heya no doa wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: It opened with nobody touching it, as far as Sora could see. Mochi had opened it.
Sora opened it himself so he could look for Mochi in the room.
It was the front door that came open, so Mochi might get out.

questions.explanation: Line 12: doa ga aita is aku, the door opening with nobody doing it, as Sora watches. Mai guesses at once (line 13: doa aita? sore, mochi da yo), and in line 14 Sora sees who did it: mochi ga doa aketa, akeru with Mochi as the one doing it. B would be doa aketa (akeru) with Sora as the doer, but he says doa ga aita. C mixes up the doors: this is the room door (heya no doa); the front door was shut and locked (line 10).

questions.english: Yuki is staying over at your place. From her futon she asks, "ne, genkan daijoubu?" (Hey, is the front door okay?) You checked a minute ago and found it shut. Tell her the door's shut.
questions.kana: ね、げんかんだいじょうぶ？
questions.answer: Say how the door is, with shimaru in its -teru form: un, daijoubu. doa shimatteru yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。ドア閉まってるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's fine. The door's shut.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、見たよ。ドア、閉まってた。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I checked. The door was shut.

questions.explanation: A door that is shut is doa (ga) shimatteru, the -teru form of shimaru: Mai asks doa, honto ni shimatteru? in line 9, and Sora checks and answers doa shimatteru in line 10. Doa shimeta (shimeru) would mean you shut it yourself, but you only found it shut. Doa ga shimeteru isn't Japanese: with ga, the verb is shimaru.

questions.english: You're leaving for work. Kenta isn't up yet and says, "boku, mou chotto nete kara deru ne." (I'm going to sleep a bit more, then head out.) Ask him to lock up when he goes.
questions.ja: 僕、もうちょっと寝てから出るね。
questions.kana: ぼく、もうちょっとねてからでるね。
questions.romaji: boku, mou chotto nete kara deru ne.
questions.answer: Ask him to lock up with kagi o kakeru, casually kagi kakete ne. The thing you put on is kagi (the lock), not the door.

modelAnswers.ja: わかった。じゃあ、鍵かけてね。
modelAnswers.english: Okay. Lock up, then, all right?

modelAnswers.ja: うん。出たら、鍵かけてね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. Lock up once you're out, okay?

questions.explanation: Locking up is kagi (o) kakeru: you put the lock on, so the object is kagi, not doa. Mai says it in line 7 (genkan no doa wa kagi kakete ne) and line 15 (genkan wa kagi kakete ne!), and Sora panics about it in line 8 (kagi kaketa kke?). Kagi shimete ne is just as common in casual speech. Not kagi kakatteru: that's the state, 'it's locked', which is Sora's reply in line 16.

questions.english: At the end, Mai tells Sora once more to lock the front door. What does he say back?
questions.ja: ソラくんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'm locking it right now, I told you!
I've locked the door (rokku suru), I told you!

questions.explanation: Line 16: kagi kakatteru, the -teru form of kakaru: the lock is on. Sora found it that way in line 10 (kagi mo kakatteru yo), so he's describing how it is, not doing anything. A, kaketeru, is kakeru, the act, so it would mean he's locking it right now, which he isn't; said with ga (kagi ga kaketeru), it's the usual mistake for 'it's locked'. B, rokku suru, is mostly for cars and phones, and it makes the door the thing you lock; at the front door it's the kagi that kakaru.

newWords.english: room (heya no doa = the door to the room)
entrance hall of a home, where you take your shoes off (genkan no doa = the front door)
Mai's cat's name (mochi is rice cake)
name suffix for a younger man or a boy (sora-kun)
